hypothesis: Known training/evaluation leakage and post-freeze mutation can be made fail-closed by a deterministic corpus manifest binding exact and normalized content hashes, source lineage, provenance, explicit independently assigned semantic-family identity, one bound semantic-audit receipt, split identity and one complete manifest root.
strongest_counterhypothesis: A manifest can create false confidence if semantic-family discovery is incomplete, caller-controlled, contaminated, the bound audit receipt is not itself verified, or the real corpus pipeline bypasses the gate; therefore the mechanism cannot itself establish semantic decontamination or final training-data acceptance.

live_external_evidence.source: Soft Contamination Means Benchmarks Test Shallow Generalization (arXiv:2602.12413)
live_external_evidence.claim_used: semantic duplicates can evade string-space decontamination and materially confound benchmark generalization estimates

live_external_evidence.source: Simulating Training Data Leakage in Multiple-Choice Benchmarks for LLM Evaluation (arXiv:2505.24263)
live_external_evidence.claim_used: controlled leakage changes evaluation reliability and motivates contamination checks before benchmark release

live_external_evidence.source: The Emperor's New Clothes in Benchmarking? (arXiv:2503.16402)
live_external_evidence.claim_used: benchmark reformulation/mitigation strategies do not universally balance contamination resistance and fidelity

self_falsification_delta.finding: V1 initially declared semantic family assignment external but did not mechanically bind the family map to a concrete audit artifact.
self_falsification_delta.repair: Require semantic_audit_receipt_hash per row, require one shared audit snapshot for the complete freeze, and include that audit hash in the manifest root.
self_falsification_delta.remaining_limit: The freeze gate binds the audit identity but does not verify the audit receipt content or correctness of semantic-family discovery.
